summary: Tetris entries from Sami's spine and the prepared candidate backlog, built for per-platform route research.

entries.title: Tetris DS

emulation.notes: Use melonDS or original DS hardware with readable dual-screen layout.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Good: accurate DS emulation with dual-screen constraints.

primary.why: Nintendo DS is the platform, so the original DS release is the complete archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the original Nintendo DS cartridge in melonDS or original hardware; preserve the dual-screen layout and final local/offline modes.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Nintendo DS release; melonDS preserves dual-screen presentation cleanly.
all_releases.reason: primary: only release platform for this entry.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No alternate platform release is sourced for this entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection-era online features are historical; preserve local/offline content in the DS release.

entries.title: Tetris

emulation.emulator: Official Digital Eclipse emulation/recreation in Tetris Forever
emulation.notes: No separate emulator stack is needed for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official modern recreation of the original text-mode Electronika 60 version.

primary.why: Tetris Forever includes an accurate recreation of Alexey Pajitnov's first 1984 Electronika 60 version, while the Windows release gives the cleanest modern capture route and collection-level documentary context.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Electronika 60 recreation inside Tetris Forever on Windows. Capture with integer scaling or clean fullscreen, and treat the other included games as historical context rather than replacements for this 1984 entry.

all_releases.fidelity: Original text-mode hardware version; historically authoritative but impractical for normal capture.
all_releases.reason: skip: original hardware is the content source, but the sourced Tetris Forever recreation is the accessible modern primary route.

all_releases.platform: Mainframe / early PC and computer ports
all_releases.fidelity: Early licensed and circulated ports vary by hardware and ruleset.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful for historical comparison, but they are not as accessible or cleanly documented for a single archive playthrough as Tetris Forever's 1984 recreation.

all_releases.platform: Tetris Forever on Windows / Switch / PlayStation / Xbox / Atari VCS
all_releases.fidelity: Modern official collection with the 1984 Electronika 60 recreation and clean capture on current hardware.
all_releases.reason: primary: best sourced fidelity/accessibility route for the original Tetris while preserving the 1984 version as the target content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Tetris has many historically important variants, but for the 1984 base entry the sourced official recreation is the clearest primary route; Game Boy/NES/Sega variants should be handled as separate entries when queued.

entries.remaster_caveats: Tetris Forever is not a complete substitute for every famous Tetris variant; it is used here specifically because it includes a sourced recreation of the 1984 Electronika 60 original.
